title: Two-step SCWL process comparator and credit-supply stress integration
hypothesis: A matched one-step versus two-step SCWL comparison may reveal a Pangola-specific accepted-liquid benefit, while separate credit-supply and interest-rate stress accounting may improve FIN-001 milestone financing decisions.
mechanisms: Subcritical-water pretreatment followed by supercritical liquefaction, compared against a matched one-step control
Separate interest-rate shocks from credit-availability/drawdown/covenant shocks in milestone tranche accounting
baseline: Matched one-step SCWL Pangola batch and baseline project-financing ledger using actual counterparty terms when available.
combined_output_contract: Accepted liquid-fuel quality and MJ per dry feedstock with complete mass/energy/cost closure; for finance, same milestone plan with principal, rate and credit availability varied independently.
expected_gain: Potential process-design information and improved finance-risk decomposition; no gain measured.
negative_effects: two-step pretreatment may add energy/water costs
bio-crude yield is not accepted fuel yield
India empirical finance results do not transfer directly to Thailand or this project
uncertainty: High: publisher full texts/supplements inaccessible in this cycle; source data and project-specific experiments absent.
falsifier: Reject two-step SCWL if accepted-fuel yield/quality or total cost does not improve under matched boundaries; reject finance benefit if it double-counts principal or infers lower WACC without counterparty evidence.
rollback: Keep current one-step process as baseline and preserve separate rate/credit scenarios without promoting them to forecasts.
next_experiments: Retrieve full ACS Energy & Fuels article and supplement; pin methods/data/licenses.
Reproduce source reference case where possible, then run randomized matched Pangola one-step/two-step batches.
Close mass, carbon and energy balances through final accepted fuel.
Retrieve full Emerging Markets Review tables and identification details.
Add rate-only, credit-only and joint stress scenarios to FIN-001 using documented counterparty terms.
nonclaims: No Pangola yield or accepted fuel
No project interest saving or WACC reduction
No new physical law or QPU advantage
